input.title: BH | Premier Kensington Leather Chest of Drawers — In Espresso
input.descriptionHtml:
In a Kensington townhouse, dressing for the evening has its own small ceremony: a shirt laid out, cufflinks chosen, a watch set down on top of the chest before the jacket goes on. This chest is made for that ritual. Its four drawers keep shirts, ties and folded things in good order, and a shelf pulls out from just below the top, giving you a place to lay out a watch, a wallet and the evening's tickets.

The wood case is covered in leather and outlined with rows of brass tacks, with brass handles to pull each drawer, in the spirit of campaign furniture, the travelling chests made to be carried from place to place. It is a compact 40 inches wide, so it suits a dressing room or a narrow bedroom wall, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a bedroom or dressing room with a valet tray, a lamp and a mirror hung above, or in a study, where the pull-out shelf makes a handy place to pour a drink. This listing is for one chest of drawers.

input.title: BH | Premier Saint-Antoine Shagreen Dresser
input.descriptionHtml:
In eighteenth-century Paris, the craftsman Jean-Claude Galuchat made shagreen the finish of choice for the things people handled every day: cases, boxes, the small pieces reached for each morning. This dresser carries that idea into the bedroom at full scale, made for the daily routine of dressing and putting away. Its eight drawers give a whole wardrobe of folded things a place, and its leather, embossed with shagreen's pebbled grain, is a finish made for daily hands.

Beneath the leather is a wood case, and large ring pulls give each drawer an easy grip. At more than six feet wide it makes one long, low run of storage with a broad top above it, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set it along the wall facing the bed with a lamp at one end, a tray for watches and rings, and a mirror hung above it, or use it in a dining room for table linens and candles, with napkins folded and ready in the drawers. This listing is for one dresser.

input.title: BH | Premier Saint-Émilion Pine Eight-Drawer Dresser — In Driftwood
input.descriptionHtml:
When the vines around Saint-Émilion are ready to pick, the old houses fill with family for the harvest, and every drawer is needed for folded clothes and the table linen for long suppers. This dresser is made for a full house. Its eight drawers give everyone a place to unpack, and its long top has room for a mirror, a lamp and a jug of whatever is in season.

It is built in pine and stands on chamfered corner posts, posts with their sharp edges planed away at an angle, and every drawer front, the top and both ends are framed with a border of short-grain wood. Iron hardware, cast and aged to look old, gives each drawer a solid grip, and the whole piece wears a worn finish that looks lived with from the first day. It arrives fully assembled.

Give it the long wall of a bedroom, with a mirror above it and a dish for earrings and cufflinks, or let it hold tablecloths, napkins and candles in a dining room. This listing is for one dresser.

input.title: BH | Premier Quai Voltaire Shagreen Dresser — In Charcoal
input.descriptionHtml:
Dressing in a Left Bank apartment is an unhurried ritual: shutters opened onto the Seine, a shirt chosen from a neat drawer, a watch picked up from the same spot each morning. This dresser is made for that routine. Its three drawers give folded things an orderly home, and its leather, embossed with the grain of shagreen, gives each drawer front a fine texture you feel every time you open it.

The case stands on an iron base with brass accents and modern hardware, and every drawer is lined with marbleized paper, the swirled paper of old bookbinding. At 34 inches tall its broad top sits at an easy height for a lamp and a tray, whether it stands opposite the bed or beside it. It weighs 167 lbs and arrives fully assembled.

Put it opposite the bed with a small lamp, a dish for rings and a framed photograph, or use a pair flanking the bed, each with a reading lamp and the books waiting to be read. This listing is for one dresser.

input.descriptionHtml:
Gauguin and the painters who gathered at Pont-Aven in the 1880s came for the Breton light, and mornings in the village still begin with shutters folded back to let it in. This dresser is made for the start of the day: dressing in that early light, the drawers sliding open one after another as the outfit comes together. Its six roomy drawers hold a full wardrobe of folded things, and its quiet, understated design lets the light and the room do the talking.

It is made from acacia wood throughout, a dense, hard-wearing hardwood that stands up well to daily use. At five feet wide and 42 inches high it gives a broad top to dress from, with space for a lamp, a mirror and a dish for jewelry. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it opposite the bed with a mirror hung above and a jug of flowers on top, or place a pair either side of a wide bed in a large bedroom. It also works in a dining room, the drawers holding linens and candles. This listing is for one dresser.

input.title: BH | Premier Big Sky Acacia Chest of Drawers — In Chestnut
input.descriptionHtml:
In a Big Sky cabin, the morning starts with dressing for the mountain: wool socks, base layers and a warm sweater pulled from the drawer before the boots go on. This chest of drawers is made for that daily layering. Its drawers give every season's gear a place, so the thick sweaters and the summer shirts each have a home, and its broad top takes the watch, the wallet and the gloves for the day.

It is built of acacia, a dense hardwood with lively grain, and finished with handles made to look like bone, a rugged touch that suits a lodge or a ranch house. At 44 inches wide and 42 tall, it is a substantial piece that holds its ground. Acacia's grain varies from board to board, so each chest has a character of its own. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it in a bedroom or a dressing area by the mudroom, with a lamp, a tray for keys and a framed trail map hung above. This listing is for one chest of drawers.

In 1925 Germany's most famous design school moved to Dessau, and the work made in its new workshops followed one simple idea: a piece should show plainly what it is for. This chest is built on that idea, for the everyday business of getting dressed and putting away. Three wide drawers hold the clothes you reach for most, and a metal base lifts the case off the floor so it reads lighter than its size.

The case is mango wood, a dense hardwood with a lively grain, given a deep stain, and it rests on its metal base with nothing added for show. Classic pulls in brushed iron give each drawer a firm grip. It is sized for a bedroom wall, a hallway or the space under a window, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a bedroom with a lamp, a small mirror and a dish for cufflinks, or use it in a hall for scarves, gloves and the dog's leashes. This listing is for one chest of drawers.

In 1756 the French porcelain works moved to Sèvres, just outside Paris, and with Madame de Pompadour among its champions, its porcelain became part of how the court dined and furnished its rooms. This dresser is made for the first quiet minutes of the morning, when the day's clothes are chosen and a ring or a watch is picked up from the porcelain top. That inset is smooth and cool under perfume bottles and a jewelry dish, and three deep drawers below take the folded things.

The porcelain is set into the top with softly rounded corners, and the drawer fronts are trimmed with bamboo detailing and finished with round pulls that are easy to grasp. At more than four and a half feet wide it gives a generous surface to dress from, and it arrives fully assembled.

Give it the wall opposite the bed with a tall mirror over it and a lamp at one end, or put it to work in a dining room, napkins and tablecloths in the drawers and a pair of candlesticks on the porcelain. This listing is for one dresser.

In Vimmerby, the Småland town where the author of Pippi Longstocking grew up, children come in from the woods and fields with muddy boots and full pockets, straight into a painted pine hall. This hall cabinet is made for that daily arrival. Its top is a landing place for hats, mittens and whatever was found outside, and its storage takes the rest, so the hall stays clear for the next person through the door.

It is built of reclaimed pine, timber given a second life, under a painted finish, and raised ridges run from top to bottom down its front and sides, with a moulded edge finishing the top. The texture gives it the feel of an old Swedish country piece, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set it inside the front door with a basket for gloves on top and a mirror above, or in a mudroom with a lamp, a bowl for keys and the dog's leash on a hook nearby. This listing is for one hall cabinet.

Its two wide drawers hold the knits, scarves and wool socks a coastal walk calls for, and its broad top is ready for a hat, a pair of gloves and the dog's leash.

It is built of pine veneer with hand-forged iron, so the metal carries the small marks of the hammer and no two pieces are quite alike. At 232 lbs it is a weighty, solid chest, and at 32 inches tall it sits low enough to slip beneath a window or a hung mirror. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a hallway by the door with a mirror above and a bowl for keys, or in a bedroom for folded sweaters and spare blankets, with a lamp and a stack of books on top. This listing is for one chest of drawers.

Set it along a bedroom wall with a lamp, a tray for jewellery and a vase of roses, or in a hall where it keeps scarves, gloves and table linens within reach. This listing is for one chest.

Place it in a bedroom under a mirror, with a lamp, a tray for cufflinks and watches, and a framed photograph, or use it in a hall for linens, scarves and gloves. This listing is for one chest of drawers.

Use it as the heart of the living room, ringed by a deep sofa and two armchairs, and load it with a tray of glasses, a stack of art books and a bowl of figs or lemons in the middle. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier Ouray Round Mango Wood Coffee Table — In Chestnut
input.descriptionHtml:
Ouray sits so deep in the San Juan Mountains that people call it the Switzerland of America, and a day there ends the same way in any season: boots off, everyone back inside, and the whole group gathered around a low table with mugs and a map of tomorrow's trail. This round coffee table is made for that circle. With no corners, everyone pulls in close, and its broad top has room for a game, the mugs and a pair of tired feet.

It is made of mango wood, a hardwood with a lively, varied grain, worked in a geometric pattern of peaks that recalls a mountain skyline. At 42 inches across and 18 inches high it suits a deep sofa or a ring of armchairs, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set it in the middle of a den or family room with a sectional around it, a wooden board of cheese, a deck of cards and a stack of trail guides. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier Primrose Hill Square Parquet Coffee Table — In Stone
input.descriptionHtml:
In a Primrose Hill terrace house, friends drop in on the way back from the top of the hill and the front room fills up around one big table: a pot of coffee, a plate of something sweet and a board game spread out in the middle. This coffee table is built for all of it. At five feet square it gives everyone a side of their own to sit at, and there is still room in the middle once the cups and plates are down.

The pine top is laid in a parquet pattern inside a frame of beaded moulding, the small rounded edging that catches the light, and the corners are mitred so the lines run cleanly all the way around. Grooves cut along the solid pine shape its sides, and the finish leaves the pine's grain in plain view. At 18 inches high it sits at a comfortable reach from a sofa, and it arrives fully assembled.

Centre it in front of a large sofa, or between two sofas facing each other, with a tray of mugs, a stack of books and a low bowl of flowers in the middle. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier Biot Round Glass and Iron Coffee Table — In Brass with Glass Top
input.descriptionHtml:
In Biot, an evening with friends often begins on the terrace and never quite moves indoors: chairs drawn around a low table, a bottle of rosé on ice, small plates going around as the sky darkens. This round coffee table is made to sit at the centre of that gathering. Without corners, everyone can reach the middle, and its cast glass top lets the light through, so the table stays easy on the eye even at 34 inches across.

The glass is cast in a mould, which gives it a softer, deeper look than a sheet of plate glass, and it rests on a base of iron forged by hand in an aged brass finish. At just under 19 inches tall it sits within easy reach of a sofa seat, and at 141 lbs it stays put once placed. It comes in two boxes and needs assembly.

Place it at the centre of a living room, a sofa on one side and a pair of armchairs facing it, laid with a stack of art books, a bowl of figs and the evening's glasses, and the matching side tables at either end. This listing is for one coffee table.

Lincoln's Inn has the calm of a place where people read for a living, and the old rooms of the Inns of Court suggest how to live with it: leather, polished brass and a low table spread with whatever needs reading next. This coffee table brings that working calm into the living room. Its leather top is a good surface for books and papers laid out to read, and at 48 inches long it has room for the week's reading alongside the coffee.

The top is buffalo leather, a thick hide with a pronounced grain, laid over a base of finished wood, with touches of brass for a warm glint. The leather softens and darkens gently with use, taking on the look of a well-loved desk. It stands at a height that suits a sofa seat, and it arrives fully assembled.

Put it in front of a sofa in a living room or library with a tray for coffee, a stack of the week's papers and a small bowl for keys, or let it anchor a pair of leather chairs in a study. This listing is for one coffee table.

This coffee table is made for that kind of gathering. Its long top has room for cups and plates on every side, and two deep drawers open from each side, so the cards, candles and coasters are always within reach.

It is made from old pine, the body painted in the soft, worn grey of a Swedish country house and the top left in natural wood, with iron adding a quiet, sturdy detail. At 55 inches long and 32 deep it gives a full sofa and a pair of chairs something to share, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set it in front of a sofa with a coffee pot, a plate of cinnamon buns and a deck of cards, with board games and spare candles tucked away below. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier Brussels Iron and Glass Coffee Table — In Jet with Glass Top
input.descriptionHtml:
In the 1890s Victor Horta built houses in Brussels that showed what iron and glass could do in a home, with the ironwork left on view and light pouring through to every room. This coffee table brings that pairing into the living room, made for evenings when the drinks come out. Its glass top lets the ironwork show through from above, so the whole table stays light to the eye, and its broad square surface has room for glasses and small plates from every side.

The base is solid iron bar, each piece cut and welded by hand, and the top is half-inch tempered glass, heat-treated so it is far stronger than ordinary glass. At 45 inches square it suits a full sofa with chairs facing in. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Put it before a deep sofa with a tray of cocktails, a bowl of nuts and a few art books, where the iron frame reads clearly through the glass. This listing is for one coffee table.

This coffee table brings that taste to the tea tray. Its legs are shaped like bamboo, and its thick glass top gives the cups and the teapot a clear, steady surface while letting the frame show through.

The frame is iron worked to look like bamboo, the jointed cane style that was so popular in Regency England, under an antiqued finish. It carries a glass top a full half inch thick, and at 18 inches high it sits at an easy reach from a sofa. It ships in two boxes and needs assembly.

Draw it up to a sofa with a tray for tea, a bowl of peonies and a few art books, and let a patterned rug show through the glass. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.descriptionHtml:
In the low, glass-walled houses of mid-century Palm Springs, the evening starts by the pool with a shaker, a tray of glasses and the mountains going pink behind the palms. This coffee table is made for setting that tray down. Its glass top keeps the room open and full of light, the way those houses did, and its iron base looks as if it has been bent from a single sheet to hold the glass up.

The base is iron in a gold finish, its folds and straight runs drawn in clean, modern lines, and the top is a single panel of glass laid across it. At 48 by 24 inches it fits in front of most sofas without crowding the room. It comes in two boxes and needs assembly.

Set it in front of a low sofa with a pair of lounge chairs, a tray of cocktail glasses, a bowl of limes and a large book of photographs. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.descriptionHtml:
Through the 1700s the ships that sailed out of Gothenburg for Canton brought back chests of tea and crates of porcelain, and a pot and a few fine cups set out for visitors became a mark of a welcoming Swedish home. This coffee table is sized for that kind of welcome. At 39 inches square it suits a smaller living room or a pair of chairs, and its Chinese-shaped legs keep the thread of that old trade running through the room.

It is built from pine in a framed plank construction, a top of boards held within a sturdy frame, made to have the look and texture of old reclaimed timber. The finish is rubbed on by hand, which gives the surface depth and a soft glow. It arrives fully assembled.

Place it between a loveseat and an armchair in a den or a small living room, with a teapot and two cups on a lacquered tray, a plant and a book or two. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier Gothenburg Large Pine Coffee Table — In Alabaster
input.descriptionHtml:
In 1745 the East Indiaman Götheborg sank at the mouth of Gothenburg's harbour on her way home from Canton, and when divers explored the wreck in the 1980s they brought up porcelain once meant for Swedish tea tables. This coffee table brings that tea table home, at full size. At 57 inches square it has space for a pot, cups and plates of food for a whole sofa of guests, and its legs carry the curve of Chinese furniture.

It is pine in a framed construction, boards held inside a sturdy frame, made to look and feel like old reclaimed wood, with a finish rubbed on by hand for softness and depth. At 96 lbs it stays settled in place when a loaded tray is set down. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it before a deep sofa in a living room or a sunroom, with a tea tray, a vase of branches and a pile of books on one corner, and leave the middle clear for the plates when friends arrive. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier Amersfoort Round Mango Coffee Table — In Driftwood with Charcoal Base
input.descriptionHtml:
Piet Mondrian was born in Amersfoort in 1872, and the clear, ordered rooms he came to love are still the Dutch ideal: a few good things set out, nothing in the way, and plenty of space to sit and talk. This coffee table is made for that kind of room. Its round top keeps a small group of chairs close together with no corners to knock against, and at 35 inches across it holds the coffee, a few books and a jug of tulips with space left around them.

It is mango wood in a softly aged grey finish, its round top kept clean and plain so the grain carries it. At 18 inches high it sits at a comfortable reach from a sofa or a pair of armchairs, and its compact size suits an apartment living room as well as a reading corner in a larger house. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it between a sofa and two chairs with a coffee pot, a stack of art books and a vase of tulips in spring. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.descriptionHtml:
In Appledore, where the Torridge meets the sea, the fishermen's cottages are painted in bright colours and their front rooms are small and companionable, with coffee poured for whoever stops by. This round coffee table is made for that kind of easy gathering. With no corners, everyone around it is the same reach from the pot, and its 46-inch top is broad enough for cups, a plate of cookies and the morning paper spread out flat.

It is pine with a finish rubbed in by hand, which gives the surface a soft, even depth, and its lines have a relaxed mid-century feel that sits comfortably in a coastal room or a city one. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in front of a sofa with two armchairs pulled in close, holding a coffee pot, mugs, a bowl of shells and a stack of sailing magazines, with a basket of firewood or a dog's bed close by. On a wet afternoon it takes a jigsaw puzzle or a board game, with room on every side for the players. This listing is for one coffee table.

Give it the space before the sofa in a den, with the teapot and cups on a tray, a few books on London to leaf through and a small bowl of fresh flowers. This listing is for one coffee table.

Use it in front of a loveseat or between two armchairs, with a board for bread and cheese and a candle, or pair it with a small side table nearby for a lamp. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier East Hampton Coffee Table — In Salt with Charcoal Frame
input.descriptionHtml:
Summer weekends in East Hampton run on friends arriving: someone back from the beach, someone bringing a bottle, everyone ending up on the sofas with a drink in hand. This coffee table is made for the middle of that gathering. At 52 inches long it gives everyone room to set down a glass, and its simple modern lines keep the room feeling open and easy even with a crowd in it.

It is made from birch and ash with MDF under a smooth, even finish, and at 18 inches high it is a comfortable reach from a sofa seat. Its generous top is as good for a game of cards or a board of cheese as it is for a stack of books. It needs some assembly.

Set it in front of a sofa with a tray of glasses, a bowl of lemons and a stack of summer novels, or between two armchairs in a sunroom with a deck of cards and a dish of olives. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier York Reclaimed Wood Coffee Table — In Almond
input.descriptionHtml:
The medieval houses of the Shambles in York still lean over the street on their timber frames, built to be lived in hard and to last for centuries. This coffee table is made in that spirit, for the everyday business of a living room: mugs of tea, board games and feet up at the end of the day. Its long, low top has room for all three at once.

It is made from reclaimed wood, timber that had a working life before it came to this table, and at 179 lbs it is a heavy, grounded piece that stays exactly where you put it. Its low height of 16.5 inches suits a deep sofa, so a mug is always within easy reach from the cushions. It arrives fully assembled.

Centre it in front of a sofa with a tray of mugs, a stack of books and a candle, with room left at the edges for a board game on a winter evening. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier Dunster Oak Coffee Table — In Cocoa
input.descriptionHtml:
The best Exmoor walks finish at a low table: back in a cottage in Dunster with the fire lit, a teapot in the middle, scones and jam set out, and everyone leaning forward from the sofa to help themselves. This coffee table is made for that gathering. Its long oak top gives the whole spread room to sit, and it stands low enough that everyone on the sofa can reach the pot without getting up.

It is made of oak, with a long top 54 inches end to end and 28 deep, and at 103 lbs it is a grounded piece that will not shift when a tray is set down or feet are tucked up beside it. Its plain, traditional lines suit a cottage living room as readily as a newer house. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in front of the sofa with the teapot and a plate of scones, a stack of walking guides and a bowl of apples, and leave room at one end for a game of cards after supper. This listing is for one coffee table.

input.title: BH | Premier Cold Spring Turned-Leg Console Table
input.descriptionHtml:
A Saturday in Cold Spring, the river village north of New York City, means browsing the antiques shops along Main Street and coming home with something found. This console table is made for the moment you walk back through the door: the keys, the bag and the afternoon's find all need somewhere to land. Its long top, a little over six feet, holds them all, and its turned legs have the look of a piece you might have carried home that day.

It is made of pine, and its legs are turned, shaped on a lathe into rounded profiles, the detail that gives a simple table its character. At 16 inches deep it keeps a hallway clear. It arrives in one box and needs assembly.

Let it greet you in the entry hall with a lamp, a dish for keys and two old prints hung above, behind a sofa with a row of books, or in a dining room as a serving table for supper. This listing is for one console table.

Walk the Faubourg Saint-Honoré and you pass doorways where leather has been cut and stitched for generations, and the habit comes home with you: the first thing your hand touches inside the door should be something finely made. This console is made for that moment of coming in, when the keys, the gloves and the mail are set down. Its shagreen top, a leather with a fine pebbled grain, gives each of them a soft landing, and at just 12 inches deep it fits a narrow hall.

The leather covers a wood frame, and a slim trim of gold leather runs along its edges for a little shine. It stands at a good height for setting things down without bending, and its top is long enough to hold a lamp at one end and a bowl at the other. It arrives fully assembled.

Place it in an entrance hall under a mirror, with a lamp, a dish for keys and the day's mail, or set it behind a sofa that floats in the room, where it holds a pair of lamps and a few framed photographs. This listing is for one console table.

The Palais de Chaillot at the Trocadéro was built for the 1937 Paris exhibition, all clean lines and gilded figures, and the Paris of that decade knew how to make an exit: gloves on, lipstick checked, keys collected on the way out. This console is made for those last minutes at the door. Its three drawers keep gloves, keys and sunglasses in order, and its shagreen top, a leather with a fine pebbled grain, gives a handbag somewhere to land.

The top is leather in a shagreen pattern over a slim iron base in a gold-toned finish, a pairing straight out of 1930s Paris. The drawers open on neat, compact pulls in the manner of old travelling chests, and at 12 inches deep it fits a narrow entrance. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it in an entrance hall beneath a round mirror with a lamp and a dish for keys, or use it in a bedroom as a slim dressing table with a jewellery tray and a bottle of scent. This listing is for one console table.

In Hatton Garden, London's jewellery quarter, small precious things are handled with care and every piece has its own place. This console table brings that habit to the getting-dressed part of the day. Its five drawers give rings, bracelets, necklaces and watches a home each, and at only 11 inches deep it stands against a bedroom or dressing room wall where a deeper chest would crowd the floor.

It is made of pine and painted by hand, so the finish carries the soft trace of the brush. At more than seven feet long it offers a broad top for a mirror, a lamp and a jewellery tray, with the drawers set in a row along its length and one at the centre. It arrives fully assembled.

Run it along a bedroom wall beneath a long mirror, with a lamp at each end and a dish for the earrings you wear most, or behind a sofa as a slim console in the living room. This listing is for one console table.

input.title: BH | Premier Naxos Marble Console Table — In Jet with White Marble Top
input.descriptionHtml:
On Naxos the Portara, the great marble doorway of an unfinished temple to Apollo, has stood over the harbour for some 2,500 years, the first thing anyone sees on arriving by sea. This console table is made for the doorway of a house, where every arrival sets something down. Its long, narrow marble top gives keys, mail and a bowl of lemons a cool place to land, and at only 12 inches deep it fits a hall without crowding it.

The marble is white and the legs are iron wrought by hand, with turnings and curves that echo the arches of church architecture, so the base draws the eye as much as the top. Its weight keeps it planted against the wall, steady under a lamp and a stack of books. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Place it in an entrance hall beneath a mirror, with a lamp, a dish for keys and the day's mail, or behind a sofa to hold a pair of lamps and a vase of branches. This listing is for one console table.
